name: Romanian deadlift
angleNote: Hip flexion: 0° = standing, 90° = trunk about horizontal. The knees bend a little as you hinge. Lifting makes the angle smaller. Torques are per leg.

strength.note: Relative hip-extension torque vs hip flexion, assumed strongest with the hip bent. Peak is per leg, typical trained adult. Approximate.
strength.source: TODO: verify against published torque–angle data

strength.note: Relative knee-extension torque vs knee flexion, weakest near straight, strongest around 60°. Peak is per leg. Approximate.
strength.source: TODO: verify against published torque–angle data

strength.note: Relative plantarflexion torque, strongest with the calf stretched. Peak is per leg. Approximate.
strength.source: TODO: verify against published torque–angle data

muscles.name: Hamstrings
muscles.note: Lengthened as you hinge with nearly straight knees: the main target of the lift.

muscles.name: Adductor magnus
muscles.note: Rear part extends the hip, more so when it is deeply bent.

muscles.name: Erector spinae
muscles.note: Hold the spine straight against a long lever. Approximation: driven by the hip's effort.

muscles.name: Calves (soleus, gastrocnemius)
muscles.note: Plantarflexors: keep the shin from tipping forward.

phases.name: Top
phases.text: Standing tall: the bar hangs close under the hips.

phases.name: Hinge
phases.text: Hips move back while the shins tilt back slightly so the bar stays over the mid-foot.

phases.name: Bottom
phases.text: Trunk near horizontal: the hip's moment arm is largest here.

variants.name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
variants.notes: Arms hang straight down from the shoulders. The solver tilts the shins so the centre of mass of body + bar stays over the mid-foot, which is what moves the hips back. Knee flexion grows from 5° to 23° through the hinge.

variants.name: Stiff-legged deadlift
variants.notes: Knees almost locked: the shins can't help, so the hips must travel further back and the hamstrings are stretched more.
